messages:
tara: quick question — running a replay vs synthetic load comparison after the kernel selector change and seeing weird TTFT p95 spikes in the replay runs. anyone seen similar?

mike: yup. first guess: KV cache warmup/priming mismatch between replay and synth. replay preserves user prefixes so you can get micro-hotspots. synth often uses randomized short prefixes so cache hit patterns differ. :thinking:

anya: also check span sampling in the profiler. we were losing the kernel selection trace for a subset of requests after the swap — makes it look like latency jumps are unexplained. i added a small collector to record kernel decisions + batch size.

zach: can you share the collector snippet? as a first pass i'd align these: seq-length distribution, prefix length distribution, batching window / batch size, and quantization flags. apples-to-apples means matching the empirical distributions, not just mean values.

anya: sure — here's the lightweight log format i'm using (JSON lines):

```
{"req_id": "$REQ", "kernel": "attn_kernel_v2", "batch_sz": 8, "kv_hit_ratio": 0.72, "selector_reason": "latency_policy", "latency_ms": 12.3}
```

this gets emitted from the runtime right after kernel selection and after kvcache lookup. helps correlate kernel choice -> observed tail.

mike: metrics housekeeping suggestion: measure TTFT p95/p99 in two windows — cold window (first N seconds of run) and steady-state window (after warmup). compute TPOT as total time spent generating tokens / total tokens emitted (exclude prefix processing). goodput should be tokens/sec delivered to caller under no backpressure; QPS is raw requests/sec. they diverge with batching and retries. write these definitions into the bench SOP so we don't compare apples to oranges later.

tara: agreed. do we have a recommended warmup protocol? replay harness currently replays real traces without an explicit warmup phase which might be the source of noise.

zach: proposed warmup: run the first 5 minutes of trace as warmup but _don't_ record latency metrics; for kvcache have an explicit kv-warmup pass of the most common prefixes (top 1k). command i used locally:

```bash
replay-harness --mode=replay --traffic-file traces/2026-01-prod.json \n  --kv-warmup-seconds=60 --warmup-only-prefixes=top1000 --seed=42 \n  --record-after-warmup=true
```

bench-bot: benchmark run queued: bench-1766009876-apples-compare-1 (tags: replay, synth, kv-warmup) — estimated 2h

mike: another subtle thing: kernel selector nondeterminism. some kernels have tie-breakers that depend on current batch composition. we should capture the kernel_name per-request and ensure both replay and synth runs log the same selector inputs so we can compare decisions. otherwise the 'swap' might trigger different internal heuristics.

anya: for regressions, capture micro-profiles: GPU kernel times, memcpy times, and queueing delay. even a few microseconds of queueing variance can move p95 around with huge fanout. i added tags to the traces so we can filter by kernel_name and kv_hit_ratio.

tara: nice. next steps: 1) zach, run apples-to-apples A/B with the kv warmup + profiler collector; 2) mike, draft the bench SOP text for TTFT/TPOT/goodput vs QPS; 3) anya, make collector opt-in flag and ensure low overhead. i'll fold results into the perf postmortem if we see a regression. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
